hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: The effective closure of Hormuz has produced the largest supply disruption in history with over 1 billion barrels lost, visible traffic at 5-15% of pre-war levels, clandestine ghost flows providing only partial relief, stockpiles declining fast, and Trump rejecting any shared oversight on June 10 — the disruption thesis is not just intact but intensifying.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: May CPI confirmed at 4.2% YoY — the highest since April 2023 — with energy accounting for over 60% of monthly gains, core CPI at 2.9% and rising, Fed funds stuck at 3.50-3.75% with zero cuts priced for all of 2026, and the FOMC split 8-4 at the last meeting: a textbook stagflation lock-in with no policy exit visible.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Hyperscaler capex is confirmed at $725B for 2026 with capital intensity at 45-57% of revenue and Morgan Stanley projecting $1.5T in new debt over three years, yet AI has produced no measurable GDP impact, capex is materially outpacing cloud revenue growth, and circular capital flows between AI startups and hyperscalers mask the absence of genuine external monetization — bubble risk is structurally elevated but a hard break has not yet occurred.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold has corrected from its $5,405 January peak to $4,094 today — a drawdown of roughly 24% — pressured by higher-for-longer yields, a stronger dollar, and ceasefire noise, though S&P Global confirms gold has not broken below the ~$4,400 structural floor until today, suggesting the current level represents a deeper flush that warrants downgrading confidence even as central bank demand and geopolitical fragmentation provide underlying support.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: S&P Global confirms the 2026 copper average price forecast remains above $12,100 per tonne despite macro headwinds, with a cumulative structural deficit of roughly 3 million tonnes projected by 2036 and concentrate markets tight for years, but recent hawkish Fed repricing and dollar strength have driven near-term price pressure that keeps this pillar in WATCH territory.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Meta signed agreements for up to 7.8 gigawatts of nuclear capacity for AI data centers, Microsoft renewed contracts for 800 megawatts of dedicated nuclear supply, the DOE awarded $900M to General Matter for HALEU enrichment capacity as part of a $2.7B initiative, Denison Mines received final regulatory approval for the Wheeler River project in Canada, Italy moved toward restoring a nuclear legal framework, and uranium spot held at $86.1 per pound on June 9 — the renaissance is broad-based and accelerating.

ALAB.note: ALAB hit an all-time high of $372.37 on June 3 before pulling back to $330.86 today — the AI connectivity thesis is operationally intact with Q2 2026 revenue guidance of $355-365M implying 87% YoY growth and new Scorpio X-Series design wins — but ALAB is trading at 34.77x forward Price-to-Sales versus the sector average of 7.02x, Northland downgraded to Market Perform on May 23, top insiders executed a major stock sell-off in mid-May, and at P/E 78.65 in a stagflation regime the valuation has fully outrun the thesis.

POWL.note: The data center electrical equipment thesis remains structurally valid given confirmed $725B hyperscaler capex, but POWL at P/E 38.16 with the broader industrials sector under pressure from higher-for-longer rates and a VIX spiking above 22 creates near-term multiple compression risk with no new catalyst visible today.

MOD.note: Negative FCF of -$101M is a direct contradiction of the stagflation thesis — in a 4.2% CPI environment with higher-for-longer rates, cash-burning industrials face compounding cost pressure — and there is no evidence today of a FCF inflection that would rescue this position.

GFS.note: The CHIPS Act thesis remains unvalidated with no new catalysts today and GFS continues to trade as a show-me story — the geopolitical reshoring narrative is intact in theory but the stock offers no near-term earnings trigger to compress its P/E of 29.71.

CRDO.note: Credo is riding the same AI connectivity wave as ALAB with strong revenue momentum, but the lack of FCF and high valuation mean it has drifted from a growth-at-reasonable-price thesis toward a pure-momentum trade vulnerable to any AI capex sentiment shift.

ARM.note: ARM at P/E 100.21 with only $750M FCF is priced for perfection in a regime where the Fed has frozen rates, core PCE is running at 4.18%, and VIX has spiked to 22.22 — the royalty model thesis is intact but the entry price remains indefensible on any risk-adjusted basis.

S.note: SentinelOne is showing genuine fundamental improvement with a path to profitability and positive EPS trajectory, but at $14.79 with P/E 29.91 the cybersecurity spending environment under stagflation is uncertain and the stock lacks a near-term catalyst to break out of its range.

ZS.note: Zscaler with $1.1B FCF and 26% ARR growth YoY to over $3B is the strongest fundamental name in the WATCH list, but the AVOID signal reflects valuation compression risk in a higher-for-longer rate environment — the thesis has drifted from pure-play ARR growth to a value-relative-to-peers argument, which is a weaker base.

AXON.note: AXON at EV/EBITDA of 379 with only $63M FCF has experienced complete thesis drift — it was originally held as a defense-adjacent public safety play but is now priced as a hyper-growth software platform, and in a stagflation regime with VIX at 22.22 and zero Fed cuts priced, holding a name at 379x EBITDA with negligible cash generation is indefensible.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.
